title: Building blocks
slide_intent: Teach designers to see which elements make an identity recognizable and which allow variation. A clear inventory helps them choose a combination appropriate to the message.
strategic_value: Special Olympics can give local teams room to vary imagery and color while retaining a common mark and typographic system.
demonstration: The page defines the mark’s elements alongside primary and secondary colors, type, curve and photography. Annotated tiles at right turn those terms into visible specimens.
practical_value: Use the inventory to identify the core mark elements, then select the supporting type, palette and photography for the communication.

content_islands.name: Introduction
content_islands.spec: Place the gray section label and red heading above the brief purpose statement.

content_islands.name: Element definitions
content_islands.spec: Use two columns for descriptions. Group symbol, logotype and program name at left, and the palettes, type, curve and photography beside them.

content_islands.name: Identity specimens
content_islands.spec: Build an annotated cluster of tiles at right. Connect cyan labels to the wordmark, symbol, program name, palette samples, typeface, curve and photographs.
